html:
Basil II was Byzantine emperor from 976 to 1025, the longest reign of any Byzantine emperor. Known as the Bulgar-slayer, he left the empire at its greatest size since the 7th century. He was the son of Romanos II of the Macedonian dynasty, and two generals, Nikephoros II and John Tzimiskes, ruled while he was a child.

His early reign was a fight to survive. He lost to the Bulgarians at the Gates of Trajan in 986 and faced great revolts by the generals Bardas Skleros and Bardas Phokas. To beat Phokas he made a deal with Prince Vladimir of Kiev: 6,000 warriors in exchange for marriage to Basil's sister Anna, if Vladimir was baptised. That led to the baptism of Rus' and the Varangian Guard.

He then spent decades conquering the Bulgarian state of Tsar Samuel, winning at Kleidion in 1014 and annexing all Bulgaria by 1018. He also pushed the eastern border into Armenia and Georgia. He left a full treasury but no son. Under his brother and his nieces, among them Zoe, the empire began to slip.
